name: 2018 livery
description: White fuselage; the whole fin and the rear fuselage under it dark Lufthansa blue, the blue starting on a straight diagonal that runs from the fin's leading edge down and forward to the belly. A white crane in a thin white ring on the fin. Dark-blue 'Lufthansa' over the forward windows, a small blue crane-in-ring under the cockpit. White engines; white winglets with a small blue crane-in-ring.

sources.note: The 2018 livery (introduced February 2018; the blue darkened and the yellow dropped from the tail).

logos.description: The Lufthansa crane (Kranich): a stylised flying crane, wings raised in a V, neck stretched forward, inside a thin ring; white line art on the dark blue.
Small dark-blue crane in a ring under the cockpit windows.
Small dark-blue crane in a ring near the top of the sharklet's outer face.

titles.style: Lufthansa Head: a bold, slightly tight grotesque, mixed case, upright, over the forward windows.

notes: Small details not drawn: yellow squares by each door, a Star Alliance star by the cockpit, the type and the aircraft's city name small under the forward windows, the registration and German flag ahead of the blue block. On widebodies (A350, 787, 747-8) the blue block's diagonal starts further aft, following the fin's leading edge. February 2018 to 2019 the first repaints had a lighter blue and some kept the yellow ring; by 2026 most of the fleet wears this scheme; some older airframes still fly the pre-2018 scheme (white, blue fin with a yellow disc and blue crane), e.g. Lufthansa Cargo's 777F D-ALFA in July 2025. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on two A320neos (D-AINX 2025, D-AINO 2023) fitted to the measured A320 shape: the blue block's forward edge is straight seen from the side, which round the fuselage is a curve: drawn as points along it (smooth), 0.2-0.4 m from the first drawing; the title's baseline sits just above the windows (y 0.345, not 0.24) with a cap height of 0.31; the fin ring a little larger and further aft. The title's face measured 2026-11-20 on D-AINX and D-AINO (each face set as the title, its letter outlines against the photo's): Lufthansa Head's letters are wider and heavier than Helvetica's, and Montserrat ExtraBold follows them closest on both photos, so it comes first.
history: Replaced Skyarium v1's approximation (a yellow tail band from the pre-2018 scheme). The 2018 livery replaced the 1988 Otl Aicher scheme (gray belly, blue fin with a yellow disc).
